title: Hearing Office Facilities Note: Large Hearing Rooms for Unemployment Insurance Appeals
content:
One hundred employees is the mark for a large hearing room at the Department hearing office under Unemployment Insurance Appeals. For an in-person session, large hearing room days are allowed by the size of the appellant's workforce, read from the appellant's latest quarterly contribution and wage report on its Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts record — the employee count it reports for the reference day of the quarter's third month — together with whether the appeal has a granted subpoena request.

**Rule.** The large hearing room days are the large-room-with-witness days for an appellant whose latest quarterly contribution and wage report counts at least the large-room employee count on the reference day of the quarter's third month and whose appeal has at least one granted subpoena request, the large-room days for an appellant whose latest quarterly report counts at least the large-room employee count and whose appeal has no granted subpoena request, and zero days for an appellant whose latest quarterly report counts fewer employees or who files no quarterly report. These days are added to the room block gap, and the set hearing date is moved later by the total before the calendar-day rule is applied.

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Large-room employee count | 100 employees (third month of the quarter, on the latest report) |
| Large room with witness | 5 calendar days |
| Large room | 2 calendar days |

## Days by report and subpoenas

| Latest quarterly report: employees in the quarter's third month | Granted subpoena request on the appeal | Large hearing room days |
|---|---|---|
| 100 or more | at least one | 5 |
| 100 or more | none | 2 |
| fewer than 100 | any | 0 |
| no quarterly report filed | any | 0 |

## Points of judgement

- The report read is the latest quarter's report, and within it only the third-month employee count; the first- and second-month counts do not decide.
- *Boundary:* a third-month count of exactly 100 reaches the large-room count; 99 does not.
- An appellant that files no quarterly report receives 0 days.

*Hypothetical cases:* latest report shows 140 employees in month three and one subpoena request granted — 5 days; the same report with only a pending, undecided subpoena request — 2 days; latest report shows 85 employees — 0 days.
